To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the antibody specificity of antisera raised against acid-treated bacteria of E. coli and S. minnesota is dependent on the acid used and that the antigenic determinants of LipA-Ae and LipA-HCI differ in their accessibility for antibody binding.

the antibody specificities of antisera raised against HCl-treated Re mutant bacteria are identical for both antigens LipA-Ac (diacylated lipid A) and LipA-HCI (monophosphoryl lipid A), whereas the antibodies in antisera raised against acetic-treated bacteria are directed to different antigenic determinants present in both antigens.

the phosphate ester bonds of the free lipid A of Gram-negative bacteria are involved in the expression of antigenic determinants, and that the glycosidic linkage of the phosphate ester bond is of importance for the recognition of the antigen by antibodies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of two distinct antibody specificities recognizing two different antigenic determinants of lipid A.
the development of a new type of vaccine, based on lipid A of E.coli, which is devoid of endotoxin activity and which can induce a protective immune response.
the characterization of two different antibody activities directed against free lipid A, which recognize two different antigenic determinants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the antigenic structure of LipA-Ae differs from that of LipA-AHCl, and that both antigens possess different antigenic determinants.
the antibody specificity of the antisera depends on the nature of the acid employed in the immunogen preparation, which in turn determines the antigenic structure of the lipid A.

the antibody specificities obtained with both antisera were directed toward the phosphate groups of the lipid A backbone, but that these antibodies differed in their recognition of phosphate groups of the different lipid A molecules.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
two different antibodies were obtained, each recognizing a distinct antigenic determinant of free lipid A.
the antigenic determinants recognized by these antisera are located in the disaccharide moiety of LipA-HCL and in the disac-charide moiety of the 4'-phosphate group of LipA-Ae.
two different antigenic determinants are present in free lipid A, which are recognized by different antibody specificities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is important to characterize the antibody specificities obtained after immunization with acid-treated lipopolysaccharide.
the phosphate groups of lipid A are important for antibody binding, but that the phosphate groups do not have to be in a glycosidic linkage.
it is possible to obtain antibodies against different antigenic determinants of the same lipid A molecule by varying the preparation of the immunogen.
